logs.intro: nexcrate records here what it does. Messages are always in English, which makes them easier to look up online when troubleshooting.

mode.title: How much gets recorded?
mode.intro: Something is always recorded, the level only decides how much. Normal is enough for everyday use. Turn on more for a while when you are tracking down a problem.
mode.label: Log level
mode.descNormal: What happened, plus warnings and errors.
mode.descDetailed: Also the details of every step.
mode.descTrace: Everything nexcrate can record. A lot of lines, meant for troubleshooting only.
mode.question: How long should “{{mode}}” stay on?
mode.fixed: The level is fixed by the environment variable {{variable}} and cannot be changed here. If you want to switch it here, remove the variable and restart nexcrate.

lines.title: Messages
lines.levelHint: Shows the chosen level and everything more important.

clear.title: Clear the log?
clear.text: All lines so far will be deleted. This cannot be undone. If you still need them, download the log first. New messages keep being recorded.

account.title: Account
account.intro: The one account you use nexcrate with.
account.languageHint: Applies on every device you log in on.

password.title: Change password
password.intro: Afterwards all other devices are logged out. This one stays logged in.
password.mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
password.done: Password changed. All other devices have been logged out.

sessions.title: Logged-in devices
sessions.intro: Log out everywhere ends the login on all devices, including this one. That helps if you forgot to log out on someone else's device.

twoFactor.title: Second factor
twoFactor.intro: After the password, nexcrate also asks for a code from an authenticator app such as Aegis, 2FAS or your password manager. A sign-in through a provider uses the provider's second factor.
twoFactor.offText: Off. The password alone opens nexcrate.
twoFactor.scan: Scan the code with your authenticator app.
twoFactor.manual: If that does not work, type in this key:
twoFactor.qr: QR code for the authenticator app
twoFactor.codesOnce: Your recovery codes. Each one opens nexcrate exactly once if the phone is missing. They appear only now: keep them somewhere safe.
twoFactor.fileHeader: nexcrate: recovery codes. Each code works exactly once.
twoFactor.recoveryIntro: The current codes stop working afterwards.
twoFactor.disableIntro: Afterwards the password alone opens nexcrate again.

signIn.title: Sign-in through authentik
signIn.intro: Sign in with your account at authentik or another OpenID Connect provider. nexcrate links exactly one account at the provider and turns every other one away.
signIn.linkedNow: Linked. From now on you can sign in through the provider.

authentik.title: Set up authentik for me
authentik.intro: nexcrate creates the provider and the application in authentik and lets in only the account the token belongs to.
authentik.tokenHint: Create one in authentik under Directory, Tokens and App passwords with the intent API. nexcrate uses it for this setup only and does not store it.
authentik.blueprintHint: Rather without a token: the blueprint creates the same in authentik. Then enter client ID and secret by hand.
authentik.done: authentik is set up and lets in only {{owner}}. Now link your account.

byHand.intro: For authentik, Authelia, Keycloak, Pocket ID and others. Create an application there with the redirect address below.
byHand.secretKept: Leave empty to keep the stored secret.
byHand.name: Name on the button

signIn.redirectHint: This is how it must appear at the provider. Behind a proxy, enter the address to the outside.
signIn.notLinked: Not linked yet. Sign in at {{name}} once, that account then opens nexcrate.
signIn.passwordLoginHint: Off: only the provider opens nexcrate. If it fails, NEXCRATE_PASSWORD_LOGIN=1 in the compose file opens the sign-in with a password again.
signIn.emergency: NEXCRATE_PASSWORD_LOGIN=1 is holding the sign-in with a password open right now, whatever the switch says.

account.emergencyOnly: Applies only to the emergency access while the sign-in with a password is off (NEXCRATE_PASSWORD_LOGIN=1).

about.title: About nexcrate
about.intro: Movies, shows and music in one place, with several versions per title.
about.versionUnknown: The version cannot be read right now.
about.tmdbText: Titles, overviews and posters come from The Movie Database (TMDB).
about.tmdbNotice: This application uses TMDB and the TMDB APIs but is not endorsed, certified, or otherwise approved by TMDB.
about.xemText: When releases count a series or an anime differently from TMDB, the mapping of the numbers comes from TheXEM, a community project.
about.musicText: Artists, albums and tracks come from MusicBrainz, covers from the Cover Art Archive. Files without usable tags are recognized through AcoustID.

outside.title: Address to the outside
outside.address: nexcrate can be reached at this address
outside.addressHint: Such as https://example.com/nexcrate. Other programs build “open in nexcrate” from it. Leave it empty when nexcrate runs only at home under its own address.
outside.noBase: nexcrate runs without a sub path. The environment variable NEXCRATE_URL_BASE sets one, after a restart.
outside.base: nexcrate runs under the sub path {{base}} (NEXCRATE_URL_BASE).

update.title: New version
update.switch: Look at GitHub once a day
update.switchHint: Only the newest release is asked for; nexcrate sends nothing about itself.
update.off: Switched off: nexcrate never asks GitHub.
update.notFound: GitHub has no release yet, or the repository is not public.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.intro: nexcrate sends its events to another program, signed with a secret only you and the program know. Nexview needs none; it reads the event stream itself.
webhooks.name: Name
webhooks.urlHint: http or https. It may carry a token of the receiver; the log names only host and port.
webhooks.secretOnce: You see the secret only now. Enter it at the receiver.
webhooks.signature: Every delivery carries X-Nexcrate-Signature: t=<time>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of “<time>.<body>”>.

bazarr.title: Bazarr
bazarr.intro: Bazarr finds subtitles. It only knows Radarr and Sonarr, so nexcrate answers it as both: movies as Radarr, series as Sonarr.
bazarr.hint: Off until you switch it on. On, Bazarr may read the library with a key, and nexcrate records the subtitles Bazarr writes so they move with their video.
bazarr.beta: Beta: built against Bazarr 1.6. nexcrate imitates part of Radarr's and Sonarr's API, so a Bazarr update may break the connection until nexcrate catches up. If it does, please tell us on GitHub.
bazarr.inBazarrIntro: In Bazarr, switch on Settings, Radarr and Settings, Sonarr and enter these values. The two differ only in the base URL. Address and port are the ones this page runs under; when Bazarr runs in the same Docker network, the container name often fits better.
bazarr.key: API key: give Bazarr a key of its own with nothing but Read, the same for both parts. Bazarr sends it in the address, as it does to Radarr.
bazarr.noteVersions: Every version is an entry of its own in Bazarr, so a movie in 1080p and in 4K shows up twice. The version's name comes along as a tag, and Bazarr can give each tag a language profile of its own.
bazarr.noteSubtitles: Subtitles Bazarr writes next to a video go where the video goes: renamed with it, into the recycle folder with it on an upgrade or a removal. Switching on looks once for subtitles that are already there.
bazarr.notePaths: If Bazarr sees the media under other paths than nexcrate, enter path mappings in Bazarr.
